plan.title: Liver QuantSeq 3' treated vs control DE + GSEA
plan.analytical_narrative:
The input is a single raw integer gene-level count matrix (counts.csv, 12000 genes x 6 samples, gene symbols in the first column) from STAR/featureCounts, with metadata.csv giving one condition label per sample: 3 treated vs 3 control human liver samples, unpaired, single batch. The research question is simply which genes differ between treated and control, so the plan is a two-group count-based differential expression analysis followed by a ranked pathway readout.

Two facts from the profile drive the method choices. First, the library is Lexogen QuantSeq FWD 3' tag-seq: one read per transcript molecule at the 3' end, so a gene's count carries no transcript-length dependence. The counts therefore go into the model exactly as they are — no length correction, no tximport, and no length-normalized unit (TPM/FPKM) anywhere in the analysis. Because a 3' library gives long genes fewer reads than a full-length library at the same depth, the pre-filter floor is lowered to 5 counts (rather than the conventional 10) in at least 3 samples, the smallest group size; DESeq2's independent filtering then does the rest at the results stage. Second, 3 replicates per group is a low-power design. DESeq2's Wald test with apeglm shrinkage is used at the default alpha of 0.05 with BH adjustment; the threshold is not loosened to compensate, and the report states explicitly that at n=3 both count models recover only a minority of true effects — mostly large fold changes — so absence from the significant list is not evidence of no change. edgeR's quasi-likelihood F-test is run on the identical filtered matrix and design as a robustness check, with the intersection treated as the high-confidence set.

Step order: T1S1 does sample-structure QC (blind VST, PCA on the 500 most variable genes, sample distance heatmap, library sizes) before any test, so an outlier or a sample that fails to group with its condition is visible before it silently drives the fit. T1S2 runs the filter, model, Wald test, apeglm shrinkage and BH/independent filtering, and inspects the p-value histogram before trusting the adjusted values. T1S3 runs the edgeR QL cross-check. T2S1 takes the full ranked list of every tested gene — ranked by the DESeq2 Wald statistic, the chosen side of the disputed ranking-metric question, because it scales the effect by its uncertainty and does not saturate into ties — and runs fgsea against MSigDB human hallmark (present in the store at 2026.1), then GO BP as the follow-up collection; Reactome is not staged, and the step must say so rather than substitute silently. Over-representation is deliberately not planned: with n=3 the significant list will very likely fall below the ~50-gene floor where a hypergeometric test has no power. T1S4 consolidates everything with the required fit diagnostics, effect columns (unshrunken LFC, shrunken LFC, lfcSE), method/version/threshold record and sessionInfo.

Low count pre-filter for 3' tag library
~ condition with explicit reference level control, raw counts, no length correction
fgsea preranked GSEA on the DESeq2 Wald statistic against MSigDB Hallmark, then GO BP
Consolidated report with MA plot, dispersion plot, p-value histogram, power statement, leading edge genes, sessionInfo
Low count filter: keep a gene with at least 10 counts in at least the smallest group size of samples

steps.name: Preranked GSEA on the Wald statistic
steps.question: Which hallmark and GO biological process gene sets are coordinately shifted between treated and control liver, on the full ranked list of tested genes?

steps.context: Downstream of the 3-vs-3 treated versus control DESeq2 contrast on human liver QuantSeq data. MSigDB human hallmark 2026.1 and MSigDB human GO BP 2026.1 are both present in the reference store; Reactome is not staged, so the GO BP branch takes the follow-up role and the absence of Reactome must be stated rather than silently substituted.

steps.name: Consolidated DE and enrichment report
steps.question: What is the defensible answer to 'which genes differ between treated and control' in this 3-vs-3 human liver QuantSeq experiment, with its power limits stated?
steps.description: Assemble the final report. Before any gene table, state the expected power at 3 replicates per group: at this size count-based tests recover only a minority of true differentially expressed genes, concentrated among those with fold changes above roughly two, so a gene absent from the significant list is not shown to be unchanged. Then give the method and package versions, the design formula ~condition, the contrast (condition, treated, control) with the reference level named, the alpha and BH threshold, the number of genes tested after filtering out of 12000, and the number of DE genes. Include the two fit diagnostics — MA plot and dispersion plot — plus the p-value histogram from T1S2. The gene table carries the unshrunken log2 fold change, the apeglm-shrunken log2 fold change and lfcSE for each gene; rank genes and draw plots on the shrunken value, never on the unshrunken estimate alone. Report the DESeq2/edgeR overlap from T1S3 with the intersection as the high-confidence set. For the enrichment, report the collection and its version, the ranking metric (Wald statistic), the universe, the size window, and the leading-edge genes of each reported set with their gene-level statistics, marking leading-edge overlap between reported sets. State that enrichment results depend on the method chosen. Note the 3' tag-seq library type and that length-normalized units do not apply. Close with the reproducibility record: sessionInfo, package versions, the random seed used in the enrichment permutations, and the gene set collection version.
steps.context: Final synthesis for a 3 treated vs 3 control human liver QuantSeq FWD 3' tag-seq experiment. The honest headline is constrained by power, and the report must say so before it lists genes.
